---
title: "Quiz: Group summaries and figures"
---

[Exercises](13-group-summaries.qmd) · [Lecture slides](../lectures/13-group-summaries/lec.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** A table has 24 plants in two treatment groups. After
`group_by(treatment) |> summarise(mean_mm = mean(growth_mm))`, how many rows
should the summary have? What does one row mean?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
A grouped summary produces one result per group.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**Two rows**, one per treatment. Each row describes a group; it is not an
additional plant observation.
:::

---

**Q2.** Which table supplies each layer in a plot showing individual dots and
group-mean diamonds?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The individual layer and summary layer have different observational levels.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The plant-level table supplies individual dots. The grouped summary table
supplies one mean diamond per treatment.
:::

---

**Q3.** Why use horizontal jitter with `height = 0` for a growth dot plot?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The vertical position encodes the measured growth.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Horizontal jitter separates overlapping dots without changing their
measured growth heights. Vertical jitter would move the displayed measurements.
:::

---

**Q4.** A histogram looks two-peaked with bins 2 mm wide and one-peaked with bins
6 mm wide. What can you conclude about the two peaks?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Small-sample histogram shape depends on how nearby values are grouped.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The apparent two-peak detail is sensitive to bin choice. Compare the
individual points and describe broad features that remain stable rather than
claiming two biological populations from this display alone.
:::

---

**Q5.** A caption says “Bars show error.” What information is missing? If the
figure has only individual dots and mean diamonds, what should its caption say?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Identify the plotted quantity, units, observation unit, and symbol meanings.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
An error bar must specify its quantity, such as SD or a confidence interval.
For this figure, state that dots are individual plants, diamonds are group means,
and growth is measured in mm; include available sample sizes. There are no
error bars to describe.
:::
